label: mid copy phase of long sequences, strongest when a v is about to be output
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (100% of mass): about 0 on original inputs and on the delimiter, and only on repeat inputs (in_first=0). It peaks in the middle of the copy phase (recall_idx 3-4, to_go 3-5) and gets more frequent as L grows (L=9 holds 59% of mass, L<=5 is nearly silent). The strongest modulator of magnitude is an upcoming v: when next_out is v the rate is 7.1x, and the top activations come at the 1-4 steps before v is output, then fall off once the v runs are being emitted. When v is among the next 1-4 outputs, the predicate covers 53% of top-quartile activations but only 16% of bottom-quartile ones. Other upcoming tokens (s, i, x, l, w) raise it more weakly. Within the mid-copy window it fires diffusely at low magnitude, so precision is low (about 0.27). It is too broad a mid-copy state to separate cleanly with these variables.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the next token to output (most: v, s, i, x, l, n; least: z, 0, -, p) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: v, s, w, t; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9, phase=2, recall_idx=7.
